newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks lend 400 mln yuan for Shanghai subway.
newsitem.headline: China banks lend 400 mln yuan for Shanghai subway.

text.p: A group of five Chinese banks are leading a group of banks in lending 400 million yuan to build a second subway line in Shanghai, China's biggest and fastest growing city, Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
It is the third time the group has extended loans for the building of the new line, it said.
It did not give details of the length of the loans or the interest rates.

Shanghai's second subway line will connect Shanghai's Hongqiao International Airport with a new airport in the city's premier economic development zone of Pudong, across the Huangpu River from the city centre, it said.

The group comprises the Shanghai branch of the Construction Bank of China, the Pudong branches of the Industrial and Commerical Bank of China, the Agricultural Bank of China and the Bank of China, and the Pudong Development Bank, it said.

Pudong airport is one of 32 airports in China's current five-year plan totalling around $5 billion. It is 30 km east of the city and is due to open in 2000 with a single runway and terminal capacity of 20 million passengers.
The $1.5 billion Phase 1 will provide nose gates for 34 aircraft, with subsequent phases involving three more parallel runways and three more terminals, according to press reports.

The existing Hongqiao airport is 15 km (9.3 miles) from the city and is reportedly close to its current capacity of 11 million passengers a year, with expansion planned to increase it to 13 million, the reports said.
